youtube.title: A Cow Didn't Start the Great Chicago Fire. A Reporter Made It Up.
youtube.description:
The Great Chicago Fire of October 1871 began in a barn behind Catherine O'Leary's home. Newspapers blamed her cow for kicking over a lantern, and some called her a drunk; she was an Irish immigrant at a time of strong anti-Irish prejudice. Decades later, reporter Michael Ahern admitted he and two colleagues invented the cow story 'to add color'. In 1997, the Chicago City Council officially cleared her and her cow.

📂 Case File #051: Mrs. O'Leary's Cow

Sources: Mental Floss, "Did a Cow Really Cause the Great Chicago Fire?" https://www.mentalfloss.com/history/misconceptions/did-cow-really-cause-great-chicago-fire ; The Irish Times, "Catherine O'Leary, the Irishwoman blamed for starting the Great Chicago Fire" https://www.irishtimes.com/life-and-style/abroad/catherine-o-leary-the-irishwoman-blamed-for-starting-the-great-chicago-fire-1.2983646
